blocks.value: Every company owns valuable things and also owes money to others. These are called Assets and Liabilities.
Imagine This: You own a house worth ₹80 lakh and have ₹10 lakh in savings. These are your assets. If you still owe ₹20 lakh on a home loan, that's your liability.
Assets include cash, buildings, machinery, inventory and investments. Liabilities include loans, unpaid bills and other financial obligations.
A manufacturing company may own factories worth hundreds of crores while also having bank loans used to build those factories.
Strong companies usually have valuable assets and manageable liabilities.
